people.label: patient
people.other_allele: intron 14+1delG (maternal), described as a splice mutation causing exon 14 skipping
people.key_phenotypes: first pyoderma gangrenosum at age 3 with relapses; nodulo-cystic acne; early-childhood disseminated infections (impetigo, otitis media, balanitis, molluscum); leukocytosis 33 x 10^9/l during the episode at age 3; granulocyte CD18 9% of reference

quotes.quote: Here we report our long-term observations of a 26-year-old man who had his first PG at the age of 3 and later developed relapsing PG and nodulo-cystic acne.

Eventually, LAD-1 was genetically confirmed in the patient in 2008 by one of us (DR) who found 2 heterozygous mutations in the ITGB2 gene, one splice mutation from the mother (intron 14+1delG) and one point mutation from the father (c.130A>C; p.Thr44Pro).
The patient was found to be compound heterozygous for 2 ITGB2 mutations, a known cause of LAD-I (7).
At 16 months of age, the patient contracted pertussis followed by disseminated impetigo with fever, otitis media, balanitis and extensive molluscum contagiosum infections.
Low-grade fever, leukocytosis (33 × 109/l; normal range 3-9 × 109/l) and an elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) (116 μg/l; N: < 4) were noted.
A diagnosis of juvenile PG was made and treatment with prednisolone, sulfasalazine, zinc sulphate and isoxacillin was initiated and maintained for one year.

phenotype_specificity.statement: 24995649: early-onset recurrent pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, childhood infections and reduced granulocyte beta-2 integrins; the authors say the picture is incomplete for LAD-I. PAPA syndrome was considered and PSTPIP1 testing found no abnormality. 22134107 gives no per-person features.

functional.statement: 24995649 (patient cells): granulocytes of the patient showed reduced beta-2 integrin expression (CD18 9% vs reference > 95%), with normal respiratory burst and phagocytosis; granulocytes of both parents and the sister had normal expression (relatives and a laboratory reference interval as controls). The authors judged this consistent with moderate, incomplete LAD-I. 22134107 types the c.130A>C row as LAD-I^o (< 5%).

quotes.quote: Investigations of granulocyte function revealed a reduced expression of ß 2-integrins, normal expression of Fcγ-receptors and selectin receptors, a normal respiratory burst and a normal phagocytosis (Table I, Table SI1 , Fig. S21 ).
In contrast, granulocytes from the patient's parents and sister demonstrated a normal expression of ß 2-integrins (see Table I).
These findings were consistent with moderate and incomplete LAD-I.
However, the expression of ß 2 -integrins on granulocytes is abnormal in consistence with a leaky, hypomorphic LAD-I disease.

In this nomenclature the superscript symbol indicates whether the protein is present at < 5% of normal expression (^o), diminished in expression (^−), i.e. between 5% and 20% of normal expression, or normally present but nonfunctional (^+)

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense variant, p.(Thr44Pro), from the batch HGVS. 24995649 suggests the Thr44Pro substitution may preserve some residual CD18 expression and function (a hypomorphic allele), while the maternal splice allele is expected to abolish expression. The paper describes LAD-I as autosomal recessive and caused by decreased expression or function of CD18 (beta-2 integrin).

quotes.quote: The mutations are predicted to replace threonine-44 in CD18 by proline (father's mutation) and to cause skipping of exon 14 from CD18 mRNA, leading to a frameshift and premature termination of CD18 protein synthesis (mother's mutation).
This last mutation will almost certainly lead to absence of CD18 protein expression, but the Thr44Pro substitution may preserve some residual CD18 protein expression and function.
However, the expression of ß 2 -integrins on granulocytes is abnormal in consistence with a leaky, hypomorphic LAD-I disease.
Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].

authors_classification.statement: 24995649 calls the two ITGB2 variants 'novel mutations' and a 'known cause of LAD-I' (citing 22134107); no formal classification. 22134107 lists c.130A>C in Table 1 'Mutations in the LAD-I gene ITGB2'.

concerns: 22134107 is a mutation-database update: the variant appears only as a Table 1 row with an accession number, with no case description, sex, clinical phenotype, zygosity or parental testing. (Applies to A0090 and A0091.)

Probable same person, not merged by the pipeline: 22134107 accession A0090 (LAD1-ID0402) carries c.130A>C and c.2080+1delG; the 24995649 patient (LAD1-ID0072) carries c.130A>C and 'intron 14+1delG' (intron 14 is c.2080_2081 in 22134107). Dirk Roos (DR), who genotyped the patient in 2008, is an author of both papers; 24995649 cites 22134107 as its ref 7, and 22134107 lists c.130A>C as unpublished.
Contradiction if they are the same person: 22134107 types the c.130A>C row LAD-I^o (< 5% CD18), but 24995649 reports CD18 9% on granulocytes and 'moderate and incomplete LAD-I' (the LAD-I^– range).
24995649 describes the patient as clinically atypical for LAD-I (no umbilical, wound-healing or periodontal problems; no basal leukocytosis). PSTPIP1 was tested and normal.
The mother (carrier of the other allele) has recurrent synovitis of unknown cause; she is not a carrier of c.130A>C.
A0091 has c.850G>A as co-listed allele; that row carries footnote c (revertant changes in lymphocytes in some carriers [32]); not checked for A0091.
24995649 writes the maternal allele in legacy intron notation ('intron 14+1delG'), not HGVS; 22134107 writes it c.2080+1delG.
22134107 numbers cDNA from the A of the ATG (+1), which matches the batch numbering; it names no RefSeq transcript (it mentions GenBank M15395 only for the offset).
notes_for_panel: Best-documented case is the 24995649 patient: compound heterozygous with parental phase, unaffected sister without either allele, and reduced CD18 on patient granulocytes. A0090 is very likely the same person, so the count of independent carriers is probably 2 (A0090/patient and A0091), not 3.
